title: Why Koreans Hike in Full Designer Gear

slides.headline: Koreans dress for Everest to walk up a 300-meter hill.
slides.note: There is a reason, and it is not the mountain.

slides.headline: Ride the subway at 7am on a Saturday
slides.body: The car fills with neon technical jackets, trekking poles and hiking boots. None of them are going to Everest. Most are going to a hill inside the city.

slides.headline: Korea is mostly mountain
slides.body: Roughly 70% of the country is mountainous. In Seoul you are never more than a short bus ride from a trailhead. Hiking is not a trip you plan. It is a Saturday.

slides.headline: Outdoor wear became fashion
slides.body: Through the 2000s, Korean outdoor brands turned hiking gear into a mainstream clothing category. The jacket stopped being equipment and became something you were seen in.

slides.headline: Hiking is a group activity
slides.body: Company clubs, university alumni groups, church groups, neighborhood groups. For a lot of Koreans over 40, the hiking club is the main standing social calendar of the week.

slides.headline: The gear is a signal
slides.body: Showing up in a t-shirt and sneakers reads as not taking the group seriously. The full outfit says you prepared, you belong here, and you intend to keep up.

slides.headline: Here is the reframe
slides.body: The outfit is not sized to the difficulty of the trail. It is sized to the seriousness of the occasion. It is closer to a team jersey than to safety equipment.

slides.headline: of South Korea is mountainous terrain
slides.body: Bukhansan, inside Seoul city limits, draws millions of visitors a year and is often cited as one of the most visited national parks per unit of area in the world.

slides.headline: So why the $500 jacket
slides.body: Because the mountain is the venue, not the point. The people on it are the point.

caption:
Ride a Seoul subway at 7am on a Saturday and it fills with people dressed for an expedition. They are going to a hill inside the city.

About 70% of Korea is mountainous, hiking clubs are a standing social calendar for millions of people, and the gear works as a signal that you take the group seriously. The jacket is closer to a team jersey than to safety equipment.

fact_check: The ~70% mountainous figure is the standard cited range (roughly 63-70% depending on the definition used). Keep the tilde.

The Bukhansan 'most visited national park per unit area' line traces to a Guinness-style claim from 2011 and is repeated widely without recent verification. Phrase it as 'often cited', which the slide does.
The $500 figure in the hook is illustrative of premium outdoor pricing, not a measured average.
